parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Today, we are going to look at how the phenomenon known as gamification has really exploded in recent years
So what exactly is gamification? It has been defined as the use of games thinking and mechanics in non-game situations, such as for business. Up to now, its most common function has been marketing. It is extremely popular with big companies, but as we'll see, it also has many other uses. Gamification techniques work on our natural desire for competition. One way they do this is by providing a reward. For example, badges or points or providing a type of virtual currency. But don't be fooled into thinking the concept is a novel one. Just think of the frequent flyer incentive schemes that were initiated by airlines to try and retain customers. In fact, it's been around for years. However, it has become more prolific with advances in technology.
So how is gamification being used? Well, it is seen as an excellent way of obtaining almost instantaneous feedback through common social media sites. However, there are other areas where it is increasingly being used. In particular, as a means of trying to convince people through fun activities to alter their behaviour. Another use is in education or training in the workplace, especially when it is just not feasible to train people on the real thing examples of this are the aircraft simulators used by pilots or the urban simulators used by town planners.
So let's look at a few examples of the successful implementation of gamification. One perhaps surprising use of gamification has been in official campaigns by governments and authorities who have quickly seen its potential. In Australia, the government developed a smartphone app called My Fit Buddy, whose aim was to help people get off the sofa and exercise. The app provided plenty of motivational content to ensure people got the encouragement they needed to increase their levels of activity. Overseas in one city, instead of just punishing the drivers caught driving too fast, a local authority conducted a trial where they rewarded good drivers with free entries into a draw. The trial was so successful that it resulted in a 22% reduction in speeding.
Gamification is also playing its part in helping people make healthy choices. In an attempt to get commuters to walk instead of using the escalators in an underground station, the staircase next to it was transformed into a piano. It had a touchpad underneath which played notes as people stepped on it. When it was in use, almost everyone opted to use the stairs instead of the escalator. Another example is a medical research company in Australia. They realised the potential of gamification to help the elderly recover much more quickly from accidents. When the elderly fall, the most common injury is not to the arm or the leg but to the hand. So they took an already popular computer game which involved people smashing fruit and adapted it so patients could practice their fine motor skills in a fun way.
Now, there are a number of things to consider when using gamification. First of all, there is no way it can work unless it is fun. In fact, without that element, it could have the complete opposite effect on the consumer. In addition, as companies are often obtaining a lot more personal information and data on their customers this way, they should always be mindful of their legal obligations in terms of legislation relating to privacy. So now, it is over to you to think of other examples of gamification that you might have come across.

analyses.content: 听到 "Up to now"（到目前为止）和 "most common function"（最常见的功能）时，紧跟着的名词就是它的主要用途。
So what exactly is gamification? It has been defined as the use of games thinking and mechanics in non-game situations, such as for business. Up to now, its most common function has been marketing.
不要听到前面的 "business" 就填上去，题目中已经有了 "In business"，这里问的是具体的业务职能。
But don't be fooled into thinking the concept is a novel one. Just think of the frequent flyer incentive schemes that were initiated by airlines to try and retain customers.
不要填 "schemes" 或 "flyer"，那是奖励计划的名称，不是使用该计划的主体（机构）。
题目中的 "first used by"（被……首先使用）对应录音中的 "initiated by"（由……发起），发起者即答案。
So how is gamification being used? Well, it is seen as an excellent way of obtaining almost instantaneous feedback through common social media sites.
不要填 "social media"，录音说的是 "through social media"（通过社交媒体），它是渠道而不是获取的对象。
题目中的 "get... quickly" 对应录音中的 "obtaining almost instantaneous..."，中间的核心名词就是获取的内容。
However, there are other areas where it is increasingly being used. In particular, as a means of trying to convince people through fun activities to alter their behaviour.
注意 "behaviour" 是不可数名词，不要加 s；另外美式拼写 "behavior" 也是正确的。
题目中的 "persuade... to change"（说服……去改变）对应录音中的 "convince... to alter"（让……信服去改变），改变的对象即答案。

Another use is in education or training in the workplace, especially when it is just not feasible to train people on the real thing examples of this are the aircraft simulators used by pilots or the urban simulators used by town planners.
不要填 "aircraft"，那是模拟器的类型（aircraft simulators），而不是使用者。
题目中出现了 "simulators used by..."（模拟器被……使用），并列连词 "and" 后面是 "town planners"，你需要填前面的那个使用者。
题目中的 "encourage people to... more" 对应录音中的 "help people... and..."，其中具体的动作动词就是答案。
In Australia, the government developed a smartphone app called My Fit Buddy, whose aim was to help people get off the sofa and exercise.
不要填 "activity"，虽然录音提到了 "increase their levels of activity"，但填在 "to ______ more" 后面，动词 exercise 语法更通顺。
In an attempt to get commuters to walk instead of using the escalators in an underground station, the staircase next to it was transformed into a piano.
不要填 "touchpad"，那是钢琴下面的装置，不是楼梯整体变成的东西。
题目中的 "worked like a..."（像……一样运作/变成了……）对应录音中的 "transformed into a..."，变形后的物体即答案。
When the elderly fall, the most common injury is not to the arm or the leg but to the hand.
这是一个典型的否定陷阱，录音说了 "not to the arm or the leg"，所以这两个都不能填，要填 "but" 后面的。
题目中的 "hurt their..."（伤了他们的……）对应录音中的 "injury... to the..."，注意听转折词 "but" 后面的部位。
Now, there are a number of things to consider when using gamification. First of all, there is no way it can work unless it is fun.
不要填 "work"，那是结果；这里的形容词 "fun" 才是让游戏化生效的关键属性。
题目说 "important... to be"（重要的是要……），录音用双重否定 "no way it can work unless it is..."（除非……否则没法用）来强调这个必要条件。

In addition, as companies are often obtaining a lot more personal information and data on their customers this way, they should always be mindful of their legal obligations in terms of legislation relating to privacy.
不要填 "legislation"，那是 "laws" 的同义词，而不是法律所涉及的具体内容。
题目中的 "laws regarding..."（关于……的法律）对应录音中的 "legislation relating to..."，其后的核心名词就是答案。
